faqs.question: What does AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Pyrazinamide measure?
faqs.answer: This test measures the susceptibility of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) complex to the drug Pyrazinamide.

faqs.question: Why is AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Pyrazinamide done?
faqs.answer: • To determine if the bacteria causing tuberculosis will respond to the drug Pyrazinamide • To guide appropriate treatment for tuberculosis • To help prevent the development of drug resistance • To monitor the effectiveness of ongoing TB treatment • To ensure optimal patient care and reduce transmission of TB

faqs.question: When is AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Pyrazinamide recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test is recommended for individuals • suspected of having tuberculosis, • with a confirmed diagnosis of tuberculosis, • undergoing treatment for tuberculosis, or • who may have been exposed to tuberculosis.

faqs.question: What if the results of the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Pyrazinamide are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results indicate that the bacteria are resistant to Pyrazinamide, which may require alternative medications for effective treatment.

faqs.question: What to expect during the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Pyrazinamide?
faqs.answer: During the test, your healthcare provider will collect a sample from a pure culture of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The sample will be sent to the laboratory for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Pyrazinamide?
faqs.answer: • Your doctor may provide specific instructions for collecting the specimen. Inform them if you have any specific requirements. • Follow any additional instructions provided by your healthcare provider regarding diet, medication, or other specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Pyrazinamide?
faqs.answer: • AFB smear: This test detects the presence of acid-fast bacilli in a sample, helping confirm the diagnosis of tuberculosis. • AFB culture: This test isolates and identifies Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex from a sample. • Drug susceptibility testing: This determines the susceptibility of Mtb complex to multiple anti-TB drugs, guiding appropriate treatment.

faqs.question: What is the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Pyrazinamide also known as?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis Drug Susceptibility Testing for Pyrazinamide or TB Antibiogram for Pyrazinamide

faqs.question: What is tuberculosis (TB)?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also involve other organs. Symptoms may include coughing, fever, weight loss, and night sweats. TB can be treated with a combination of medications for several months.
